gaps.sentence: You ___ have seen her face when she heard the news!
gaps.explanation: 'Should have seen' emphasizes how remarkable something was: should have.

gaps.sentence: You ___ take an umbrella — the forecast says heavy rain all day.
gaps.explanation: 'Should' recommends a sensible action: should take.

gaps.sentence: She ___ have received your email — her inbox was full last week.
gaps.hint: ruled out as a past possibility
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' plus the participle rules out a past possibility: can't have received.

gaps.sentence: I ___ have known you were in hospital — nobody told me.
gaps.explanation: 'Couldn't have' means it was impossible to do: couldn't have known.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: After three attempts, she ___ pass her driving test at last.
gaps.explanation: A specific past success takes 'was able to' or 'managed to': was able to pass.

gaps.sentence: ___ I borrow your charger for a minute?
gaps.explanation: 'May' is the polite way to ask permission: May I borrow.

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.
